subject: psychology
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 21–29 carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each) and questions 30–32 carry 4 marks (four parts of 1 mark each).
Section B: questions 33–38 carry 2 marks (30–50 words), questions 39–44 carry 3 marks (50–80 words) and questions 45–48 carry 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define (i) absolute threshold; (ii) difference threshold.
questions.answer: (i) Minimum physical energy needed to produce a sensory experience. (ii) Minimum change between two stimuli that can be recognised.

questions.q: Differentiate intrinsic and extrinsic motivation in one line each.
questions.answer: Intrinsic motivation comes from within, from enjoyment of the task; extrinsic motivation is based on external rewards such as money and grades.

questions.q: Name the four stages of Piaget's cognitive development.
questions.answer: Sensori-motor, pre-operational, concrete operational, formal operational.

questions.q: Who listed the developmental tasks of adolescence and how many?
questions.answer: Robert Havighurst listed ten tasks.

questions.q: Name any two internal changes of ageing.
questions.answer: Changes in respiratory, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular and central nervous systems (any two).

questions.q: Name any two features of effective communication.
questions.answer: Common frame of reference, mutual interest, common language, common environment (any two).

questions.q: What is confirmatory bias?
questions.answer: The tendency to search for information that supports one's beliefs and to ignore that which does not.

questions.q: Name any two dissociative disorders.
questions.answer: Dissociative amnesia, dissociative fugue, depersonalization disorder, multiple personality disorder (any two).

questions.q: Define health.
questions.answer: A state of physical, mental, social and spiritual well-being.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Match the Erikson crisis: (i) young adulthood; (ii) middle adulthood; give (iii) the first term; (iv) the second term of the young adult crisis.
questions.answer: (i) Intimacy versus isolation. (ii) Generativity versus self-absorption. (iii) Intimacy. (iv) Isolation.

questions.q: Name the coping type: (i) planning revision for a tough test; (ii) leaving a rejecting friend and making a new one; (iii) accepting a substitute goal; (iv) blaming a tough paper for failure.
questions.answer: (i) Attack. (ii) Withdrawal. (iii) Compromise. (iv) Rationalisation (defence-oriented).

questions.q: Name four job design elements that improve performance.
questions.answer: Variety, autonomy, responsibility, feedback and task identity (any four).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name any two multiple intelligences given by Gardner.
questions.answer: Linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal or naturalistic (any two).

questions.q: How can an emotion act as a motive?
questions.answer: A frightened child cries out for help and seeks comfort and security from a parent.

questions.q: Why is the study of physical and motor development important?
questions.answer: It is the basis for personality, social and emotional development, helps bonding with the mother figure and gives mastery over the body.

questions.q: What is proxemics?
questions.answer: The use of social distance between people: intimate, personal, social and public space.

questions.q: What is Dincharya?
questions.answer: The day routine: doing activities at the right time of day, such as rising before sunrise and drinking water first.

questions.q: Why does crowding differ in a marriage party and an overcrowded bus?
questions.answer: Density may be equal but the relationship with people, duration and meaning differ, so experience differs.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain transfer of training and its types.
questions.answer: Transfer is using earlier learning in a new situation. It is positive when the first learning helps the second, negative when it interferes, and zero when it neither helps nor interferes.

questions.q: Describe parenting styles.
questions.answer: Authoritarian is demanding and controlling; permissive is indulgent; authoritative is firm and consistent with reasons; neglectful is uninvolved and uncaring. Authoritative parenting suits socialisation best.

questions.q: Explain the key elements of communication.
questions.answer: Two-way sender–receiver process, a message, commonness of understanding, modification of the receiver's behaviour and a method of giving information (words or gestures).

questions.q: Describe the functions of attitudes.
questions.answer: They help us understand the world and choose whom to approach, describe our social groups, express our identity and values, and win support and acceptance from others.

questions.q: Distinguish intrinsic and extrinsic interests with examples.
questions.answer: Intrinsic: liking painting for itself; extrinsic: doing a task for money or praise. Intrinsic interest gives a better job match.

questions.q: Distinguish Manomaya and Vijnanamaya Koshas.
questions.answer: Manomaya is the mental sheath of feelings, emotions and memories; Vijnanamaya is the intellectual sheath of imagination, knowledge, insight and discriminating decisions.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the experimental method as a scientific method. Identify the techniques used to control relevant variables.
questions.answer: The experimenter manipulates the independent variable and studies its effect on the dependent variable, with an experimental group and a control group. Organismic, situational and sequential variables must be controlled by elimination, making conditions constant, matching, counter-balancing and random assignment; experiments can be laboratory, field or quasi experiments.

questions.q: What is extra-sensory perception? Describe its types and the applications of perception in daily life.
questions.answer: ESP is perception not explained by known senses: telepathy, clairvoyance, pre-cognition and psycho-kinesis, studied by parapsychology; most psychologists doubt it. Applications: eyewitness testimony is error-prone; habituation reduces attention to familiar stimuli while creative people continue to attend; paying attention and breaking perceptual habits improve results.

questions.q: Explain the physical development and sexual maturation in adolescence.
questions.answer: Pubescence brings a growth spurt controlled by the pituitary gland (girls 10–11, boys 12–13, peak 12.6 and 14.8 years). Asynchronization occurs as bones and muscles outgrow skills; proportions change. Sex hormones (testosterone, estrogen) cause primary and secondary sex characteristics in a fixed sequence; boys gain more strength.

questions.q: List the determinants of organizational climate and explain them.
questions.answer: Structure (centralised or decentralised), technology (routine or dynamic), external environment (economic conditions) and management policies (autonomy and feedback). A positive climate gives satisfaction and productivity.
